newsitem.title: UK: Med crude tanker activity slows, as rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Med crude tanker activity slows, as rates rise.

text.p: Crude tanker fixing in the Mediterranean/Black Sea sector slowed on Wednesday after yesterday's spate of fixings. Italian shipbrokers said rates were a touch stronger with room to improve.
By mid-afternoon, Elf's chartering of the Akademik Pustovoyt was the only Aframax (80,000 tonner) seen, brokers said.
"Despite the slow activity, rates have strengthened. We're fairly optimistic -- tonnage has thinned out, and there is an underlying strength in the market.
"It seems that rates could climb up to the mid W100-teens over the forthcoming week and a half," a broker said.
Aframaxes could command W100-102.5, whilst Suezmaxes settled at last done levels of W72.
Tanker fixing in the key Middle East market remained good and rates were seen to be slightly stronger on all route out of the region.

By mid-afternoon, three VLCCs had been seen fixed out of the region. Vessels making trips to Japan lifted fractionally to W57, with rates for Eastern voyages placed at W53, up W2.25 points. VLCCs heading for the West were seen at W53.
Activity within the UKC sector remained good, with at least four Aframaxes finding employment on cross-UKC trips.
But rates were seen to be slightly softer at W100, brokers said.
Rumours circulated on Wednesday that BP was hoping to take a VLCC of Brent from the UK-Continent sector to South Africa. But, there have been no confirmations of an enquiry.
The Caribbean upcoast-U.S market saw rates fall slightly to W140, down W2.5 points, in response to a fractional increase in vessel availability within the region.
West African activity was fair, with rates on Suezmaxes placed at W62.5. VLCCs to the U.S. were unchanged at W62.5.
